quiz.q: Which tool, embedded in Anypoint Studio, creates the Mule project's folder structure and builds the deployable JAR?
quiz.explain: A Mule 4 project is a Maven project: Maven creates the standard folders, resolves dependencies and builds the JAR.

quiz.q: Where do the configuration XML files containing your flows live?
quiz.explain: `src/main/mule` holds the main logic: flows, connector configurations and error handling.

quiz.q: Where should one property file per environment (dev, UAT, prod) be kept?
quiz.explain: `src/main/resources` supplies what the main project needs to run: property files, API spec, `log4j2.xml`, certificates.
`src/test/java` is for JUnit (almost never used); `src/test/resources` holds resources for the MUnit tests.

options: The Mule runtime version the project targets (e.g. `minMuleVersion: 4.4.0`)
quiz.explain: "Mule 4.x developer" refers to the runtime version, not Studio — Studio 7.12 embeds runtime 4.4.0.

options: The project, usually the same as the project name
The organization, often its reversed domain like `com.flipkart`
quiz.explain: groupId = organization; artifactId = the project. Reversing the domain is MuleSoft's suggestion, not a rule.

quiz.q: You remove the Database module from the Mule Palette. What happens to `pom.xml`?
options: Nothing — pom.xml must be edited by hand
quiz.explain: Adding/removing a module in the palette automatically adds/removes its `<dependency>`; JARs are downloaded from the repositories.

quiz.q: In `pom.xml`, `<version>${mule.maven.plugin.version}</version>` reads its value from which section?
quiz.explain: Properties define a value once (e.g. `3.5.4`) and reuse it with `${...}`.

quiz.q: Why must two projects not share the same groupId and artifactId?
options: Maven would delete one of them
Studio cannot open more than one project
Built JARs are stored by groupId → artifactId → version, so they would collide
They would share one HTTP port
quiz.explain: Like saving `test.doc` twice in one folder, the same coordinates would overwrite each other.

quiz.q: You create an HTTP Listener configuration with the + button. Under which tab of the configuration XML is it stored for reuse anywhere in the project?
quiz.explain: Connector configurations are global elements, usable from any flow or XML file in the project.

quiz.q: You try to drag the HTTP Listener into the Process section of a flow. What happens?
options: It works as a second listener
It is converted into an HTTP Request
Studio does not allow it — the Listener is a source and works only in Source
quiz.explain: Studio enforces placement: Listener only in Source; HTTP Request only in Process.

quiz.q: How does one flow call another flow in a different XML file of the same project?
options: It is not possible across XML files
quiz.explain: Flow Reference works within the same XML and across XML files; the called flow doesn't need a source.

cards.front: Why is a Mule 4 project a Maven project?
cards.back: Maven (embedded in Studio) creates the standard structure, resolves dependencies in pom.xml and builds the deployable JAR with plugins.
The folder on disk where Studio stores all your projects (Show In → System Explorer).
Configuration XML files with flows, connector configs and error handling — the main code. Multiple XML files and multiple flows are normal.
Custom Java code — rarely used: only when no connector exists or Mule/DataWeave can't do something.
Property files per environment, `api/` (imported RAML), `log4j2.xml`, `application-types.xml`, certificates.
Configures logging (format, file names, levels). Mule uses the Java Log4j2 framework because it's built on Spring/Java.
munit: MUnit tests (used). java: JUnit tests (almost never used).
Build output — where the deployable JAR goes.
Declares the Mule runtime version, e.g. `{"minMuleVersion": "4.4.0"}`.
Runtime (server) version. Studio has its own version (e.g. 7.12 embeds runtime 4.4.0).
Project Object Model — `pom.xml` in the project **root**: identity, properties, build plugins, dependencies, repositories.
groupId = organization (often reversed domain, `com.flipkart`). artifactId = project, usually the project name.
Tells Maven the kind of application — `mule-application`.
Values defined once and reused with `${...}`, e.g. `mule.maven.plugin.version`, `app.runtime`, encoding UTF-8.
`mule-maven-plugin` packages the Mule app into a JAR; `maven-clean-plugin` cleans previous build output.
A connector/library the project needs: groupId, artifactId (e.g. `mule-db-connector`), version, classifier `mule-plugin`.
Where dependencies/plugins are downloaded from — Anypoint Exchange and MuleSoft releases. Path: groupId → artifactId → version → JARs.
HTTP and Sockets. Adding/removing modules in the palette edits pom.xml automatically.

cards.front: Three tabs of a configuration XML
cards.back: **Message Flow** (visual), **Global Elements** (reusable configs), **Configuration XML** (the generated code).
A reusable configuration (HTTP Listener config, Database config) usable anywhere in the project.
Scope where orchestration, transformation and enrichment happen. Sections: **Source, Process, Error handling**.

cards.front: Two ways to create a flow
cards.back: Drag any component onto an empty canvas, or drag the **Flow** scope from Core → Scopes.
Calls another flow and returns — in the same or a different XML file of the project.
HTTP Listener works only in Source; HTTP Request works only in Process. Studio enforces it.
